prompt:
Teams moving to Taskflow from another tracker want to bring their issues into a project in one go. Build the backend of the bulk import.

User story: as someone who may create issues in a project, I upload a file. The client parses it into rows and sends them along with a key that identifies that upload. Every row becomes an issue in the project, in file order.

Add exactly these exports:

1. `src/schemas/issue-import.ts`:

```ts
export const importIssueRowSchema = z.object({
  title: z.string().min(3).max(200),
  description: z.string().max(20_000).nullable().default(null),
  status: issueStatusSchema.default("backlog"),
  priority: issuePrioritySchema.default("none"),
  assigneeEmail: emailSchema.nullable().default(null),
  labels: z.array(z.string().min(1).max(40)).max(20).default([]),
  dueAt: isoTimestampSchema.nullable().default(null),
});

export const importIssuesSchema = z.object({
  orgId: orgIdSchema,
  projectId: projectIdSchema,
  importKey: z.string().min(8).max(64),
  rows: z.array(importIssueRowSchema).min(1).max(500),
});

export type ImportIssueRowInput = z.infer<typeof importIssueRowSchema>;
export type ImportIssuesInput = z.infer<typeof importIssuesSchema>;
```

2. In `src/types/issue.ts`:

```ts
export interface IssueImportResult {
  readonly importKey: string;
  readonly projectId: ProjectId;
  readonly issues: readonly Issue[];   // in file order
  readonly replayed: boolean;          // true when the key had been imported before
}
```

3. In `src/server/services/issue-service.ts`: `export async function importIssues(actor: Actor, input: ImportIssuesInput): Promise<IssueImportResult>`.

4. A new domain event `issues.imported` in `TaskflowEventMap`: `EventEnvelope & { projectId: ProjectId; importKey: string; issueIds: readonly IssueId[] }`, with `issueIds` in file order and published on behalf of the importer.

Acceptance behaviour

- Access: importing needs the same permission as creating an issue in that project. An `orgId` outside the actor's workspace → `TenantScopeError`; an unknown project, including a project of another workspace → `NotFoundError` (the one in `src/server/services/_support.ts`); an archived project → `AlreadyArchivedError`. A refused import creates nothing.
- All or nothing. The import is checked before anything is written. The plan's per-project issue quota applies to the whole batch: if the project's issues plus the rows would go over the plan's per-project limit, the whole import is refused with an error and nothing is created — the refusal is the same one a single create at the limit gets, and the issues are counted the same way. The batch also spends the workspace's issue-creation rate allowance, one unit per row, before anything is written; when the allowance does not cover the batch, the import is refused and nothing is created. A refused import does not use up its key: the same key uploaded again later is treated as a first upload.
- Rows: title, description, status, priority and due date exactly as given; the importer is the author; no parent and no estimate. Imported issues are numbered in file order, continuing after the highest number the project has ever used, and issues created afterwards continue after them.
- Assignee: `assigneeEmail` is matched, case-insensitively, against the email addresses of the workspace's current active members. An address that is not one of them — unknown, belonging to someone who is not a member of this workspace, or to a member who has been removed — leaves the issue unassigned. That is never an error.
- Labels: each name in `labels` is matched exactly (case-sensitively) against the workspace's own labels. A name that does not exist yet is created — once, however many rows use it — with the default colour and no description, and the issue carries every label named for it (a name repeated inside one row counts once). Labels of other workspaces are never involved, whatever their names.
- Replays: uploading a key this workspace has already imported returns the result of that first import — the same issues, in the same order, with `replayed: true` — and creates nothing, whatever the rows now say. A different key is a new import even when the rows are identical. Keys are per workspace: the same key in another workspace is unrelated. Replays must work across restarts, so imports are persisted; a freshly migrated database (the way the test suite builds one) must have whatever you add.
- Announcements: a successful import publishes exactly one `issues.imported` event for the batch and no `issue.created`; a replay publishes nothing. The batch event must give the product everything the per-issue announcements would have: the imported issues are searchable right away; the workspace's issues-used meter rises by the number of imported issues and agrees with a full recount; the audit log gets exactly one entry for the import — action `issues.imported`, recorded as the importer's action, subject kind `project`, subject id and project id the project's, metadata `{ count, importKey }` — and no per-issue entries. Nobody is notified about imported issues (an assignee is not told), and no outgoing webhook delivery is created for them, even for endpoints that subscribe to issue events. The hidden test attaches the application's event handlers exactly as the server does at start-up.

Update any visible test that encodes behaviour this change alters.

This is an `implement` task: edit the code and stop, as for a `fix` task. Do not write a summary and do not emit an ANSWER line.
notes: Implement (product spec, no bug.patch): bulk issue import. One upload (rows + client key) becomes a batch of issues under the create-issue gates applied once to the whole batch (permission, tenancy, archived project, per-project quota for the whole batch, rate allowance one unit per row), numbered in file order, assignees resolved by active-member email, labels matched exactly and created once per name, a persisted per-workspace replay ledger, and a single issues.imported event instead of per-issue announcements — while search, the issues-used meter and the audit log must still reflect the batch and notifications/webhooks must stay silent. Reference solution: 13 files, ~300 changed lines across a new zod schema, types (IssueImportResult, event map, ActivityAction) + activity zod enum + the activity label map, drizzle schema + embedded migration (issue_imports), a new repository, issue-service (importIssues), and issues.imported subscribers in search-service, usage-service and activity-service. Why it is hard: the obvious implementation (loop createIssue) violates the announcement rules (per-issue events, webhook deliveries, audit rows), the batch quota and the rate allowance; the careful implementation (repository inserts + one event) silently loses search indexing, the usage counter and the audit entry, all of which are event-driven off issue.created in the corpus and must be re-wired for the batch event; the replay ledger must be per workspace, must not be written by a refused import, and must return the original issues in order; label creation must be de-duplicated across rows (labels_org_name_idx is unique, so a second insert of the same new name throws mid-batch and breaks all-or-nothing); assignee resolution must go through active membership, not the global user table. Trap: a per-import label snapshot that is not updated when a label is created (naive C) — a single UNIQUE constraint failure on the second row that names a new label. Hidden test: 18 cases (fields + author + defaults, numbering after archived + continuation, assignee by email incl. case, unknown, removed, foreign; no assignee alerts; labels exact-match + created once + colour/description + per-row dedup + other workspace untouched; exactly one issues.imported and no issue.created; searchable; usage meter + recount; one audit entry with metadata and no per-issue rows; no webhook deliveries; replay with different rows; different key duplicates; key scope per workspace; batch quota refusal then fit then single create refused; rate allowance refusal without burning the key; permission; archived project; tenancy for org and project). Validation: pristine tsc 0 / 617 pass; pristine+hidden 18/18 fail; solution: patch -p1 clean, tsc 0, full suite 635 pass, hidden 3x 18/18; naive A (loop createIssue per row, no ledger/event/batch checks) 6/18 fail; naive B (repository inserts + one event, but no subscribers for the batch event) 3/18 fail; naive C (complete, but labels resolved against a per-import snapshot that is never updated) 1/18 fail.
